sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Richmond County, GA?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work in Richmond County. The Board of Assessors sets the value, and the Richmond County Tax Commissioner bills and collects the tax. The tax commissioner is on arctax.com, and the assessors publish notices and run the online appeal tool through the Augusta government announcement and its property search.

Richmond County is consolidated with the city of Augusta, so one government and one school system set the rates you see on a bill. The tax commissioner says it plays no part in deciding the amount of any tax, so a complaint about the bill itself goes to the elected bodies that set millage, while a complaint about value goes to the assessors.

  • Value, notices and appeals: Board of Assessors, 706-821-2310.
  • Billing, payments, homestead applications: Tax Commissioner, 706-821-2391, 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta, GA 30901.
  • Mail: P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903.

sections.h2: What does Richmond County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Richmond County covers 324.34 square miles of land and a 2025 population estimate of 206,559 in the Census QuickFacts table. The 2020 census count was 206,607, so the population has barely moved.

Roughly half of households rent. The Census puts owner occupancy at 51.2 percent, and the median owner-occupied home at $178,500 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,141 and median household income is $55,637. The mean trip to work is 21.4 minutes, short for a county this size.

For a seller those numbers mean a buyer pool with a lot of investors and first-time owners, and tax bills that are modest in absolute terms. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place or a back-tax balance still sells, but the buyer will price in whatever the county still has on file for the parcel.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 millage rates in Richmond County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner lists four net millage rates for 2026, one for each tax district. Which one applies depends on where the parcel sits, not on the owner.

One mill is $1 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value under Georgia law. The millage page notes that several authorities combine to make the total. The assessment notice carries an estimate of savings, so compare it with the bill when it arrives.

sections.h2: When are Richmond County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's due dates page lists November 30 as the due date for 2026 real estate bills and April 1 for mobile homes. Bills usually go out in August or September, according to the Augusta assessor FAQ.

A late balance picks up interest of .875 percent each month under O.C.G.A. 48-2-40, plus a one-time 10 percent penalty added after the grace period. Unpaid taxes can end in a lien and a levy, so a house with an old balance should be dealt with before listing.

If your tax is paid from an escrow account, the office still tells owners they carry the responsibility. It does not mail bills to mortgage companies, only makes the data available. After a lender change, call the new servicer and ask whether the county balance was paid.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an assessment in Richmond County?
sections.html:
File a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. For the 2026 notices mailed June 29, the posted deadline was August 13, 2026, and that window has now closed.

Appeals can go in online through the assessor's property search, by mail, by email or in person. Georgia now requires annual notices for every owner, so a notice reaches you even when the value did not change. The notice must show the value, exemptions and the right to appeal, and the 2026 version uses a new statewide format that replaced the older tax estimate tables.

  • Read the notice for the appeal deadline the day it arrives.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses nearby and photos of condition problems.
  • If you disagree with the assessors' answer, the next step is the Board of Equalization, and then Superior Court.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work in Richmond County?
sections.html:
Owners who live in the home on January 1 can claim a homestead exemption, and the application deadline is April 1. The tax commissioner receives the application and forwards it to the assessors, who decide eligibility.

Once granted, the exemption renews on its own each year. You apply again only after a change in ownership, a name change or spelling fix on the deed, or when seeking a different exemption. Refinancing does not affect it. Married couples can claim only one homestead between them, and every vehicle the applicant owns must be registered in Richmond County. Solid waste and street light fees are not covered by the exemption.

Augusta also applies a local floating homestead exemption that limits certain increases in assessed value on qualifying primary residences. Senior and other special exemptions must be applied for in person or by mail with all supporting documents. Call 706-821-2391 with questions.

sections.h2: Who pays the property tax when a Richmond County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever owns the property on January 1 owes that year's tax, but the contract can shift the liability to the buyer, and this is normally settled at closing. The tax commissioner does not prorate taxes between buyer and seller.

  • The office must bill the January 1 owner and also the new owner if the property sold during the year.
  • If the year's tax goes unpaid, a lien is filed against the property, and it names the January 1 owner unless that owner shows the deed and the closing papers within 90 days of the due date.
  • The usual proof is an acknowledgment and receipt of settlement statement.

Because the bill often arrives after a fall closing, ask the closing attorney whether the settlement statement used an estimate and who is responsible if the real bill is higher. Keep a copy of the signed settlement statement.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Richmond County house that has tax problems?
sections.html:
Yes. A balance owed to the county is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, the same way a mortgage payoff is. The title company or closing attorney requests a payoff from the tax commissioner and settles it before funds reach the seller.

Cash buyers can close without repairs or financing contingencies, which helps when the issue is an inherited house, vacant property or a lien that has started to grow. Compare any offer against a simple list sale net of repairs and carrying costs, and ask the tax commissioner for the current balance before you decide.

faqs.q: How long do Richmond County owners have to appeal a new value?
faqs.a: Owners have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. The 2026 deadline for notices mailed June 29 was August 13, 2026, so it has passed for that year. The next year's notice will show its own date.

faqs.q: When is the homestead exemption deadline in Richmond County?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 1. You must own and occupy the home on January 1 of that year. After the exemption is granted it renews automatically unless the deed or ownership changes.

faqs.q: Does the Richmond County tax commissioner prorate taxes at a sale?
faqs.a: No. The tax commissioner does not prorate between buyer and seller. Closing papers handle that split, and those papers can later serve as proof of who owes the tax.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Richmond County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest of .875 percent per month is added to the unpaid balance, plus a one-time 10 percent penalty after the grace period, as posted on the tax commissioner's due dates page.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Richmond County homestead application by mail?
faqs.a: Mail it to Richmond County Tax Commissioner's Office, P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903. The office recommends certified mail with a USPS postmark, because metered dates are not accepted as timely.
